feedback: No earlier race exists, so this feedback rests only on what the integration of this geometry required, not on measured performance. (1) The five sensors at 1 cm spacing with 12 mm footprints give a graded signal across the tape, so I could use a single linear weight set [-2,-1,0,1,2] with no special handling. (2) Because the array spans only about 4 cm and the tape is 2.5 cm wide, the line can leave the array on sharper bends. I had to choose line_loss = 'last_direction' to handle this, so the controller depends on the array staying close to the line. If the next race shows line_loss_events above zero, or completion failing on the tightest bend, the array is probably too narrow: widen the x span (for example to about 0.06 m) before changing the controller. If the race shows steering_oscillation high while line_loss_events is zero, the cause is more likely the 5 cm forward offset or the sensor spacing than the gains, so try a shorter forward offset (about 0.03 m) or a larger spacing. If the race completes with low rms_error, keep the geometry and only adjust gains. Also, with the 4.5 m course needing an average of about 1.5 m/s, if completion_time is too long, a smaller wheel_track or lower mass gives faster response, so try mass 0.6 with the same body.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events > 0 on the tightest bend, widen the sensor span to about 0.06 m (x from -0.03 to +0.03, five sensors) and keep sensor_size at 0.012, to keep the line under the array through sharp bends.

If steering_oscillation is high while line_loss_events is 0, move the sensors forward to y = 0.03 m (from 0.05) or keep the sensor pitch and reduce the body mass to 0.6 kg, to reduce oscillation at speed.
If completion_time is above about 3.0 s with completion at 1, reduce wheel_track to 0.10 m and keep the same sensor layout, so the robot turns more readily without changing the signal scale.
